Q1: How should a promote cycle skipped with `runner_wait_long` be retried on the same day? Today nothing re-runs the cycle before the next daily cron.
Choices:
A) The orchestrator poller (`orchestrate_poll.yml`, which already runs often) dispatches the cycle again, at most once an hour, only after the latest cycle skipped with `runner_wait_long` and main's tip is still unpromoted. This needs a new `workflow_dispatch` input that routes to the `cycle` job, without changing the existing `target_sha` → `promote` path. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Add more cron entries to `promote-main-to-stable.yml` (for example every 2 hours). An extra tick exits at once unless the day's last cycle skipped with `runner_wait_long`. This is simpler, but every tick takes a runner slot even when it does nothing (§26).
C) No same-day retry: drop G2 and let the next daily schedule pick the cycle up.
Q2: Should the new runner-wait skip (G1) be bounded, so that a queue that stays long cannot hold a release (including a hotfix) forever?
Choices:
A) Not bounded: skip every tick while the oldest live queued run is older than `RELEASE_GATE_MAX_RUNNER_WAIT_MINUTES`. `0` is the only way to turn it off.
B) Bounded: once the same tip has been skipped for `runner_wait_long` for longer than the existing `AUTO_RELEASE_STABLE_QUEUE_BACKOFF_HOURS` window, dispatch one cycle whatever the wait, as `runner_queue_deep` does today. The promote cycle uses the same rule. (RECOMMENDED)
C) Bounded by a new variable (for example `RELEASE_GATE_RUNNER_WAIT_MAX_SKIP_HOURS`, default 24) instead of reusing the existing window.
